transcript.text: Good afternoon, everyone. I'd like to get started on the routine check-in for 'The Last Harbor' before we lock the presentation package. I need to hear from each of you on the archive, music, and technical sides. Could we go around and share any findings or concerns related to the current draft — the digital projection, the live string trio, and the standard 16:9 screen mask?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag an important archive-license amendment I received yesterday. The amendment confirms that this festival screening of 'The Last Harbor' must use the Northlight Archive's 35mm print — not digital projection. It also requires retaining the film's original 1.33:1 image framing without cropping, which conflicts with the standard 16:9 screen mask in the current draft. And it requires displaying the exact credit 'Restored by Northlight Archive.' I haven't entered the amendment into the festival rights tracker yet, but I'm doing so now.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a major technical issue. I tested the screening room with the live-score setup this morning, and the room's pit and monitoring arrangement supports only a solo piano — not the proposed string trio. So even setting aside Julian's archive amendment, the string trio in the current draft isn't feasible in our space. I should also note that the commissioned score cleared for this performance is 'Tide Marks,' and I have not yet updated the technical run sheet to reflect any of this.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Thank you both for these critical findings. Let me make sure I have everything straight before I make my decision. Julian, the archive amendment requires three things: 35mm print instead of digital projection, original 1.33:1 framing without cropping instead of the 16:9 mask, and the exact restoration credit 'Restored by Northlight Archive.' And Nia, the screening room can only accommodate a solo piano, not the string trio, and the commissioned score is 'Tide Marks.' Both of you have pending updates — Julian, you're entering the amendment into the rights tracker, and Nia, you need to update the technical run sheet. Are there any other concerns from the archive, music, or technical sides that I should know about before I lock the package?
